text:
alex: thinking about improving our spot procurement churn — idea: coalesce short-lived backfill requests into a rolling 'pricing window' so we only rebid every Xs instead of per-request. reduces API churn and eviction noise :thinking_face:

maria: sounds promising. how do you avoid overpaying when price dips inside the window?

alex: default plan: use capacity-optimized for the window peak, switch to price-optimized only if the weekly median price < threshold and available capacity > margin. basically two-tier decision per window.

vikram: curious about interruption tail — if we batch spinups you'll get more long-lived allocations which is good, but also longer cooldown when capacity vanishes. do we want a soft-eviction fallback?

jen: soft-fallback = immediately route new jobs to lower-cost archs (e.g., T4) + queue short inference bursts to hosted fallback. keep a tiny warm pool of fastest arch for latency-critical traffic.

alex: exactly. example config sketch: ```
{
  "window_sec": 120,
  "primary_strategy": "capacity_opt",
  "secondary_strategy": "price_opt",
  "price_margin_pct": 15,
  "warm_pool": {"size": 4, "arch": ["a100","v100"], "min_uptime_sec": 300}
}
```

sasha: what's our metric for switching strategies? eviction_rate? median_spinup_time?

vikram: use combined signal: if region_eviction_rate > 0.6% OR avg_spinup > 90s for last 30m => favor capacity. else price. also factor egress/regional-cost delta.

procure-bot: allocation event: created 8 x a100 (spot) in us-west1 as backfill window 2605001234-1.

jen: network constraint check — coalescing can amplify cross-rack egress if we pick heterogenous pools. need to prefer same-az placement when serving large batch workloads.

maria: for mixed-capacity pools, how do we prevent fragmentation? our scheduler should treat GPU families as fungible tiers, not individual SKUs. map by perf class: "high","mid","low".

alex: agreed. scheduler mapping + progressive fallback: high -> mid -> low. and add anti-affinity rules to avoid spreading one tenant across too many racks when possible.

vikram: also, add short randomized jitter to rebid windows to avoid synchronized mass churn on provider side (thundering herd). 0-30s jitter per customer.

jen: can we run a 48h canary? pick one non-critical fleet and enable windowed procurement with price_margin_pct=10, warm_pool size=2. measure cost delta, eviction tail, and retry latencies.

alex: i'll spin it up. can we capture these metrics: cost_per_gpu_hour, eviction_rate_5m, avg_spinup_s, cross_az_egress_gb?

maria: yup — I'll add dashboards and alert when avg_spinup_s > 120 or eviction_rate_5m > 1%.

procure-bot: experiment created: exp-2605001234-windowed-backfill, owners: @alex @maria.

alex: thanks. i'll post a brief runbook for rollback if we see SLO regressions. :rocket:
